entry.title: India on Track for 50 GW+ Solar in 2026

link.title: India on Track for 50 GW+ Solar in 2026

entry.content:
India is on track to commission more than 50 GWdc of solar in 2026, after adding 34 GWdc in the first half, 38% above H1 2025.

Strong utility-scale and rooftop growth, plus rising storage tenders, are shaping the market. For commercial and industrial users, the case for rooftop and solar-plus-storage keeps getting stronger.
entry.summary: H1 additions were 38% above last year; full-year record expected.

entry.title: One Crore Rooftops by March 2027: Where Things Stand

link.title: One Crore Rooftops by March 2027: Where Things Stand

entry.content:
PM Surya Ghar has crossed 50 lakh installations and expects over 75 lakh households by December 2026. The government’s target is one crore households by March 2027.

Meeting it would need the recent record pace to continue or grow. For homeowners, this suggests strong vendor activity ahead — compare quotes, verify ALMM-compliant equipment and confirm subsidy steps before booking.
entry.summary: With 50 lakh done, the scheme targets a doubling in about seven months.

entry.title: Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra Lead PM Surya Ghar

link.title: Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra Lead PM Surya Ghar

entry.content:
In the latest data, Uttar Pradesh ranked first in PM Surya Ghar rooftop installations with 74,796 plants, followed by Andhra Pradesh (69,813) and Maharashtra (60,907).

State-level support, quick discom approvals and active installers make the difference. Tamil Nadu’s new top-up subsidy aims to speed up adoption here too.
entry.summary: Recent installation data shows which states are moving fastest.

entry.title: India Solar Capacity Reaches 168 GW
entry.content:
India’s installed solar capacity reached 168.04 GW as of 31 August 2026, with 3,445 MW added during August — up from about 2,443 MW in July.

Additions are rebounding after the post-ALMM slowdown. The sector’s focus is shifting toward technology choices, storage integration and long-term project performance.

entry.title: Saatvik to Add 3.6 GW Solar Cell Capacity in Odisha

link.title: Saatvik to Add 3.6 GW Solar Cell Capacity in Odisha

entry.content:
In August 2026, Saatvik Solar Industries signed an MoU with IPICOL, Odisha’s investment promotion agency, to set up an additional 3.6 GW solar cell manufacturing facility.

With ALMM List-II in force, new cell capacity is key to easing supply constraints. More Indian cell supply should, over time, stabilise availability for rooftop and commercial projects.
entry.summary: Domestic cell manufacturing gets another boost.

entry.title: PM Surya Ghar Crosses 50 Lakh Installations

link.title: PM Surya Ghar Crosses 50 Lakh Installations

entry.content:
The PM Surya Ghar scheme crossed 50 lakh rooftop solar installations in August 2026, just over two years after launch. July 2026 recorded the highest monthly installations since the scheme began.

The scheme is expected to reach over 75 lakh households by December 2026 and targets one crore by March 2027.
entry.summary: Just over two years after launch, July set a monthly record.

entry.title: Tamil Nadu Rooftop Solar Subsidy: Up to ₹1 Lakh

link.title: Tamil Nadu Rooftop Solar Subsidy: Up to ₹1 Lakh

entry.content:
Tamil Nadu has announced a residential rooftop solar subsidy that works alongside PM Surya Ghar, with a maximum combined subsidy of up to ₹1,00,000 per household. The state has earmarked ₹50 crore for the scheme.

Net metering (1:1 credit for residential systems under 10 kW) continues to apply. Check eligibility and current subsidy amounts with your installer before applying, as details can change.
entry.summary: A state top-up on the PM Surya Ghar subsidy for homes.

entry.title: India’s Solar Capacity Crosses 164 GW
entry.content:
India’s installed solar capacity crossed 164 GW at the end of July 2026, after roughly 2,443 MW was added during the month.

The ALMM-II waiver for projects commissioned from July 2026 fell from 75% to 50%, and is due to be phased out after July 2028. Monthly additions have cooled slightly after the pre-deadline rush, but the long-term trend remains strong.
entry.summary: About 2.4 GW was added in July alone.

entry.title: India Posts Record Solar Installations in H1 2026

link.title: India Posts Record Solar Installations in H1 2026

entry.content:
India added a record 27 GW of solar PV in the first half of 2026, up 49% from a year earlier, according to PV Tech.

Developers pushed to commission projects ahead of the June ALMM List-II deadline, which pulled many installations forward. Full-year 2026 additions are now expected to exceed any previous year.

entry.title: SECI Launches 1,200 MW Solar + 3,600 MWh Storage Tender

link.title: SECI Launches 1,200 MW Solar + 3,600 MWh Storage Tender

entry.content:
SECI issued a request for selection on 19 June 2026 for 1,200 MW of solar PV hybridised with 600 MW/3,600 MWh of battery storage, connected to the ISTS network.

Pairing solar with storage lets projects supply power beyond daylight hours — a growing need for discoms and industrial buyers looking for firm, round-the-clock-style supply.
entry.summary: A large hybrid tender pairs solar generation with battery storage.
